Worked example

Rectangle, pentagon, pentagon, rectangle, pentagon, pentagon, __ — what shape comes next?

Step 1: Find the core: one rectangle, then two pentagons.

Step 2: The core has finished twice, so a new core starts.

Answer: Rectangle

Key points

  • First find the repeating core, then continue it.
  • Pizza, pizza, cake, pizza, pizza, cake — after two pizzas the next shape is cake.
  • A pattern can start at a different point and still be the same pattern: star, square, circle is the same core as square, circle, star.

mcqs.q: Circle, triangle, pentagon, circle, triangle, pentagon — what are the next two shapes?
mcqs.why: The core is (circle, triangle, pentagon) and it repeats. After the second pentagon a new core starts: circle, then triangle.

mcqs.q: Rectangle, pentagon, pentagon, rectangle, pentagon, pentagon — what comes next?
mcqs.why: The core is one rectangle followed by two pentagons. The core has repeated twice, so the next shape starts a new core: a rectangle.

mcqs.q: Angel face, sunglasses face, winking face, angel face, sunglasses face, winking face, angel face, __, winking face. What is missing?
mcqs.why: The core is (angel, sunglasses, winking) repeating. In the third round, after angel face comes the sunglasses face.

mcqs.q: Pizza, pizza, cake, pizza, pizza, __ — what comes next?
mcqs.why: The core is (pizza, pizza, cake). Two pizzas have come again, so the next item completes the core: cake.

mcqs.q: Cone, cube, cuboid, cone, cube, cuboid — what is the core of this pattern?
mcqs.why: The same three shapes repeat in the same order: cone, cube, cuboid. That repeating part is the core.

mcqs.q: Blue cube, red cube, blue cube, red cube — what comes next?
mcqs.why: The core is (blue, red). After a red cube, a new core begins with a blue cube.

mcqs.q: Which pattern is the same as: star, square face, circle face?
mcqs.why: A repeating pattern stays the same if it starts at a different point of the core. Square, circle, star is the same cycle as star, square, circle.

mcqs.q: You have spheres, cones, cubes and cuboids. Which of these is a correct pattern?
options: Sphere, cone, cube, cuboid, sphere, cone, cube, cuboid
mcqs.why: A pattern must repeat the same core in the same order. Here the core (sphere, cone, cube, cuboid) repeats exactly.

mcqs.q: In the pattern (yellow triangle, green square) repeating, what is the 5th shape?
mcqs.why: Write the pattern out: 1st yellow triangle, 2nd green square, 3rd yellow triangle, 4th green square, 5th yellow triangle.

mcqs.q: What is a 'core' of a pattern?
options: The part that repeats again and again
mcqs.why: The core is the smallest part of the pattern that repeats in the same order to make the whole pattern.

lessons.title: Number Patterns and the Hundred Chart
lessons.notes_html:
Patterns on the hundred chart

On the hundred chart, the numbers in each row increase by 1 as we go from left to right. In each column, going from top to bottom, the numbers increase by 10.

Making number patterns

A number pattern is made by adding the same amount again and again: adding 2 gives 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 ... and starting from 23 gives 23, 25, 27, 29, 31 ...

Worked example

What is the next number: 41, 45, 49, ...?

Step 1: Find the difference: 45 − 41 = 4 and 49 − 45 = 4, so it is a +4 pattern.

Step 2: Add 4 to the last number: 49 + 4 = 53.

Answer: 53

Key points

  • Rows of the hundred chart: +1. Columns: +10.
  • To find the next number, first find the jump size.
  • 34, 44, 54 is a +10 pattern, so the next number is 64.

mcqs.q: In the hundred chart, how much do the numbers increase by in each column, going down?
mcqs.why: In a column of the hundred chart, each number below is 10 more than the one above it: 1, 11, 21, 31 ... So the increase is 10.

mcqs.q: In the hundred chart, how much do the numbers increase by in each row, going right?
mcqs.why: In a row of the hundred chart the numbers count forward one by one: 1, 2, 3, 4 ... So the increase is 1.

mcqs.q: Make a pattern by adding 2: 23, 25, 27, 29, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: The pattern adds 2 each time, so add 2 to the last number: 29 + 2 = 31.

mcqs.q: Make a pattern by adding 3 from 1: 1, 4, 7, 10, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: The pattern adds 3 each time, so the number after 10 is 10 + 3 = 13.

mcqs.q: Make a pattern by adding 4 from 1: 1, 5, 9, 13, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: The pattern adds 4 each time, so the number after 13 is 13 + 4 = 17.

mcqs.q: What is the next number: 41, 45, 49, ...?
mcqs.why: Find the jump: 45 − 41 = 4 and 49 − 45 = 4, so add 4: 49 + 4 = 53.

mcqs.q: What is the next number: 34, 44, 54, ...?
Count on in the +2 pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, __, 12. Which number is missing?
mcqs.why: Add 2 each time: 8 + 2 = 10, then 10 + 2 = 12. The missing number is 10.

mcqs.q: A pattern adds 10 each time and starts at 5: 5, 15, 25, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: In the hundred chart, moving down one row adds 10: 25 + 10 = 35.

mcqs.q: A pattern adds 5 each time: 10, 15, 20, 25, __. What comes next?
mcqs.why: This pattern counts in fives, so add 5 to the last number: 25 + 5 = 30.

lessons.title: Length: Metres and Centimetres
lessons.notes_html:
Long and short

Length tells us whether an object is long or short. We measure length with two standard units: the metre (m) for larger things and the centimetre (cm) for smaller things.

A metre tape is used to measure length. A metre rod is marked from 0 to 100, so 1 metre = 100 centimetres.

Which unit?

Metres: a bus is about 16 metres, a table is 1 metre. Centimetres: a pencil is about 15 centimetres, a book is about 20 centimetres, and our height is measured in centimetres.

Worked example

Measure a spoon with a ruler.

Step 1: Match the left end of the spoon with the 0 mark of the ruler.

Step 2: Read the mark at the right end of the spoon: it ends at 8.

Answer: The spoon is 8 cm long

Key points

  • 1 m = 100 cm.
  • Big things in metres, small things in centimetres.
  • Always start measuring from the 0 mark.

mcqs.q: How many centimetres are there in 1 metre?
mcqs.why: The metre rod is divided into marks from 0 to 100, so 1 metre = 100 centimetres.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used to measure the length of a bus?
mcqs.why: A bus is a large thing (about 16 metres long). Large lengths are measured in metres.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used to measure the length of a pencil?
mcqs.why: A pencil is a small thing (about 15 cm). Small lengths are measured in centimetres.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used to measure your height in this book?
mcqs.why: The book measures our own height in centimetres, the smaller unit of length.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used to measure the height of a cupboard?
mcqs.why: A cupboard is a big object, so its height is measured in metres.

mcqs.q: A paint brush ends at the 4 mark on the ruler. How long is it in centimetres?
mcqs.why: Start at 0 and read the mark at the end of the brush: it ends at 4, so the brush is 4 cm long.

mcqs.q: A comb ends at the 11 mark on the ruler. How long is it in centimetres?
mcqs.why: Read the mark where the comb ends: 11, so the comb is 11 cm long.

mcqs.q: A toothbrush ends at the 10 mark on the ruler. How long is it in centimetres?
mcqs.why: Read the mark at the end of the toothbrush: it ends at 10, so it is 10 cm long.

mcqs.q: How many centimetres are there in 2 metres?
mcqs.why: Each metre has 100 centimetres: 2 × 100 = 200 centimetres.

mcqs.q: What do we use to measure length in the classroom?
options: A metre tape or a ruler
mcqs.why: Length is measured with a metre tape (for metres) or a ruler/scale (for centimetres).

lessons.title: Comparing Length
lessons.notes_html:
Longer, shorter, equal

To compare lengths, compare the numbers — but first make sure both lengths use the same unit.

A car is 4 metres and a bike is 2 metres, so the car is longer. A pencil is 15 cm and a mobile is 12 cm, so the pencil is longer. A wall is 5 metres and a bus is 16 metres, so the wall is shorter.

Worked example

Which is longer: a pencil (15 cm) or a ruler (30 cm)?

Step 1: Both lengths are in centimetres, so compare the numbers: 30 is greater than 15.

Answer: The ruler is longer than the pencil

Equal lengths

A pencil of 15 cm and a pen of 15 cm have equal length. A football field of 100 m and a cricket ground of 100 m are also equal.

Key points

  • Compare only lengths in the same unit.
  • The bigger number shows the longer object.
  • Same number and same unit means equal length.

mcqs.q: Which is longer: a pencil (15 cm) or a ruler (30 cm)?
mcqs.why: Both are in centimetres. 30 is greater than 15, so the ruler (30 cm) is longer.

mcqs.q: A bookshelf is 2 m and a bed is 3 m. Which is shorter?
mcqs.why: Both are in metres. 2 is less than 3, so the bookshelf (2 m) is shorter than the bed.

mcqs.q: A football field is 100 m and a basketball court is 28 m. Which is shorter?
mcqs.why: Compare the metres: 28 is less than 100, so the basketball court is shorter.

mcqs.q: Which is longer: a shoe (25 cm) or a book (15 cm)?
mcqs.why: Compare the centimetres: 25 is greater than 15, so the shoe is longer.

mcqs.q: A football field is 100 m and a cricket ground is 100 m. How do their lengths compare?
mcqs.why: Both lengths are 100 m — the same number in the same unit — so the lengths are equal.

mcqs.q: A car is 4 metres and a bike is 2 metres. Which is longer?
mcqs.why: 4 metres is more than 2 metres, so the car is longer than the bike.

mcqs.q: A wall is 5 metres and a bus is 16 metres. Which is shorter?
mcqs.why: 5 metres is less than 16 metres, so the wall is shorter than the bus.

mcqs.q: A book is 20 cm and a child's arm is 45 cm. Which is longer?
mcqs.why: 45 cm is more than 20 cm, so the child's arm is longer than the book.

mcqs.q: A red shirt is 50 cm and a blue shirt is 50 cm. How do their lengths compare?
mcqs.why: Both shirts measure 50 cm, so their lengths are equal.

mcqs.q: A mobile is 15 cm and a pen is 15 cm. How do their lengths compare?
mcqs.why: Both measure 15 cm — the same number in the same unit — so the lengths are equal.

lessons.title: Length Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Joining and taking away lengths

If a length is made longer, add. If a part is removed or used, subtract. Keep the unit the same in the answer.

Worked example

A path in a garden is 8 metres long. If we extend it by 2 more metres, how long will it be?

Step 1: The path becomes longer, so add: 8 + 2.

Answer: 10 metres

Worked example

Hussain draws a line 25 cm long, then removes a 10 cm part. What is the length of the remaining line?

Step 1: A part is removed, so subtract: 25 − 10 = 15.

Answer: 15 cm

Key points

  • "Extend", "join", "total" mean add.
  • "Remove", "shorten", "remaining" mean subtract.
  • Write the unit (m or cm) with every answer.

mcqs.q: A garden path is 8 metres long. It is extended by 2 more metres. How long is it now?
mcqs.why: The path becomes longer, so add: 8 + 2 = 10 metres.

mcqs.q: A toy train is 80 cm long. One more coach of 8 cm is added. What is the total length?
mcqs.why: Add the coach: 80 + 8 = 88 cm. (The answer is in centimetres.)

mcqs.q: Hussain draws a line 25 cm long and removes a 10 cm part. How long is the remaining line?
mcqs.why: A part is removed, so subtract: 25 − 10 = 15 cm.

mcqs.q: A toy train track is 18 metres long. If 5 metres are removed, what is the length now?
mcqs.why: Part of the track is removed, so subtract: 18 − 5 = 13 metres.

mcqs.q: A pencil is 15 cm long and a ruler is 20 cm long. What is their total length?
mcqs.why: Join the pencil and the ruler lengths together: 15 + 20 = 35 cm.

mcqs.q: A highway is 500 metres long and a connector road is 250 metres long. What is the total length?
mcqs.why: Join the highway and the connector road: 500 + 250 = 750 metres.

mcqs.q: Ali runs 100 metres and his friend runs 75 metres. How much farther did Ali run?
mcqs.why: Compare the two runs by subtracting: 100 − 75 = 25 metres farther.

mcqs.q: A dress is 90 cm long. A tailor shortens it by 18 cm. How long is the dress now?
mcqs.why: The dress is shortened by the tailor, so subtract: 90 − 18 = 72 cm.

mcqs.q: Ayesha has a 60 cm ribbon. She used 40 cm of it. How much ribbon is left?
mcqs.why: Subtract the part used: 60 − 40 = 20 cm left.

mcqs.q: Shahid's father is 185 cm tall. Awais is 85 cm shorter than his father. What is Awais's height?
mcqs.why: Awais is 85 cm shorter than his father: 185 − 85 = 100 cm.

lessons.title: Mass: Kilograms and Grams
lessons.notes_html:
How heavy is it?

Mass (weight) tells us how heavy something is. We measure mass in kilograms (kg) for heavy things and grams (gm) for light things.

Examples: a bag of apples has a mass of 1 kg and meat has a mass of 2 kg. A pencil is light — about 20 gm — and a small toy car is about 30 gm.

Worked example

Write the suitable unit for the weight of a goat.

Step 1: A goat is a heavy animal.

Step 2: Heavy things are measured in kilograms.

Answer: Kilograms (kg)

Key points

  • kg for heavy things, gm for light things.
  • An orange and a cucumber are measured in grams.
  • A watermelon and a goat are measured in kilograms.

mcqs.q: Which unit is suitable for the weight of a goat?
mcqs.why: A goat is heavy, and heavy things are measured in kilograms (kg).

mcqs.q: Which unit is suitable for the weight of an orange?
mcqs.why: An orange is a light fruit, and light things are measured in grams (gm).

mcqs.q: Which unit is suitable for the weight of a watermelon?
mcqs.why: A watermelon is heavy, so it is measured in kilograms.

mcqs.q: Which unit is suitable for the weight of a cucumber?
mcqs.why: A cucumber is light, so it is measured in grams.

mcqs.q: About how many grams does a pencil weigh?
mcqs.why: A pencil is very light. The book's estimate is about 20 grams.

mcqs.q: About how many grams does a sharpener weigh?
mcqs.why: A sharpener is even lighter than a pencil. The book's estimate is about 10 grams.

mcqs.q: About how many kilograms does a seven-year-old boy weigh?
mcqs.why: A young child's weight is measured in kilograms. The book's estimate is about 22 kg (about 20–25 kg).

mcqs.q: About how many kilograms does a bag of tomatoes weigh?
mcqs.why: A shopping bag of tomatoes is a few kilograms. The book's estimate is about 5 kg.

mcqs.q: What is mass?
options: How much liquid a jug holds
mcqs.why: Mass is the heaviness of an object. We measure it in kilograms and grams.

mcqs.q: The mass of a bag of apples is 1 kg and the mass of meat is 2 kg. Which is heavier?
mcqs.why: Compare the masses: 2 kg is more than 1 kg, so the meat is heavier.

lessons.title: Comparing Mass
lessons.notes_html:
Heavier, lighter, equal

Compare masses the same way as lengths: compare the numbers in the same unit. A toy truck of 50 gm is heavier than a toy car of 30 gm. A bottle of water of 1 kg is lighter than a school bag of 2 kg.

Worked example

A bag of apples weighs 3 kilograms and a bag of oranges weighs 1 kilogram. Which has the greater mass?

Step 1: Compare the numbers: 3 is greater than 1.

Answer: The bag of apples has the greater mass

Equal masses

A box of pencils of 20 gm and an empty lunch box of 20 gm have equal mass. A sugar bag of 5 kg and a flour bag of 5 kg are also equal.

Key points

  • Compare numbers only in the same unit.
  • Tomatoes of 3 kg are heavier than potatoes of 2 kg.
  • An apple of 80 g is lighter than an orange of 120 g.

mcqs.q: A bag of apples weighs 3 kg and a bag of oranges weighs 1 kg. Which has the greater mass?
mcqs.why: Compare: 3 kg is greater than 1 kg, so the bag of apples has the greater mass.

mcqs.q: A paperclip weighs 5 grams and a pen weighs 20 grams. Which has the greater mass?
mcqs.why: Compare: 20 grams is greater than 5 grams, so the pen has the greater mass.

mcqs.q: A toy car weighs 50 grams and a toy truck weighs 75 grams. Which has the lesser mass?
mcqs.why: Compare: 50 grams is less than 75 grams, so the toy car has the lesser mass.

mcqs.q: Ali weighs 20 kg and his friend Amjad weighs 24 kg. Who is lighter?
mcqs.why: Compare: 20 kg is less than 24 kg, so Ali is lighter.

mcqs.q: A book weighs 500 grams and a bag of sugar weighs 500 grams. How do their weights compare?
mcqs.why: Both weights are 500 grams — the same number in the same unit — so they are equal.

mcqs.q: A toy truck weighs 50 gm and a toy car weighs 30 gm. Which is heavier?
mcqs.why: 50 gm is more than 30 gm, so the toy truck is heavier.

mcqs.q: A bottle of water weighs 1 kg and a school bag weighs 2 kg. Which is lighter?
mcqs.why: 1 kg is less than 2 kg, so the bottle of water is lighter.

mcqs.q: Tomatoes weigh 3 kg and potatoes weigh 2 kg. Which is heavier?
mcqs.why: 3 kg is more than 2 kg, so the tomatoes are heavier.

mcqs.q: An apple weighs 80 g and an orange weighs 120 g. Which is lighter?
mcqs.why: 80 g is less than 120 g, so the apple is lighter.

mcqs.q: A sugar bag weighs 5 kg and a flour bag weighs 5 kg. How do their masses compare?
mcqs.why: Both bags weigh 5 kg, so their masses are equal.

lessons.title: Mass Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Adding and taking away mass

When masses are put together, add. When some mass is eaten or taken out, subtract.

Worked example

A student packs 100 g of carrots and 80 g of apples in her lunch box. What is the total mass of the lunch box?

Step 1: The two masses are packed together, so add: 100 + 80.

Answer: 180 g

Worked example

Ali bought 250 g of strawberries. He ate 50 g. How many grams are left?

Step 1: Some are eaten, so subtract: 250 − 50 = 200.

Answer: 200 g

Key points

  • Keep the unit (g or kg) the same in the answer.
  • 40 kg of flour and 20 kg of rice make 60 kg in all.
  • A 20 kg bag of rice with 5 kg taken out has 15 kg left.

mcqs.q: A student packs 100 g of carrots and 80 g of apples. What is the total mass?
mcqs.why: The carrots and apples are packed together: 100 + 80 = 180 g.

mcqs.q: Asma buys 40 kg of flour and 20 kg of rice. What is the total mass of both bags?
mcqs.why: Add the flour bag and the rice bag together: 40 + 20 = 60 kg.

mcqs.q: Ali bought 250 g of strawberries and ate 50 g. How many grams are left?
mcqs.why: Subtract the part eaten: 250 − 50 = 200 g.

mcqs.q: A bag of rice weighs 20 kg. If 5 kg of rice is taken out, what is the new mass of the bag?
mcqs.why: Rice is taken out of the bag, so subtract: 20 − 5 = 15 kg left.

mcqs.q: A bag of flour weighs 50 kg. If 20 kg of sugar are added to it, what is the total weight?
mcqs.why: Sugar is added to the flour bag: 50 + 20 = 70 kilograms in all.

mcqs.q: A packet of coffee weighs 250 g and a packet of sugar weighs 75 g. What is their total mass?
mcqs.why: Add: 250 + 75. Ones: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2, carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. Total = 325 grams.

mcqs.q: A sack of potatoes weighs 15 kg. If 7 kg of potatoes are taken out, what mass remains?
mcqs.why: Potatoes are taken out of the sack: 15 − 7 = 8 kilograms remain.

mcqs.q: A box of chocolates weighs 300 g. If 250 g of chocolates are eaten, what mass remains?
mcqs.why: Chocolates are eaten from the box: 300 − 250 = 50 grams remain.

mcqs.q: A basket holds 120 g of grapes and 130 g of plums. What is the total mass?
mcqs.why: Add the grapes and the plums in the basket: 120 + 130 = 250 g.

mcqs.q: A sack weighs 90 kg. If 45 kg is removed, what mass is left in the sack?
mcqs.why: Part of the sack's load is removed: 90 − 45 = 45 kg left.

lessons.title: Capacity: Litres and Millilitres
lessons.notes_html:
How much a container holds

Capacity is the amount of liquid a container can hold. A jug that holds 8 glasses of water has a capacity of 8 glasses.

The standard unit of capacity is the litre (L). A smaller unit is the millilitre (ml). A measuring jug filled to the 1000 ml mark holds 1 litre, so 1 litre = 1000 ml.

Worked example

A glass of cold drink is filled to the 200 mark on its scale. How many millilitres is that?

Step 1: Read the scale where the drink stops: 200.

Answer: 200 ml

Key points

  • 1 L = 1000 ml.
  • Big containers are measured in litres, small amounts in millilitres.
  • A small bottle holding 1000 tiny cups of 1 ml holds 1000 ml = 1 litre.

mcqs.q: How many millilitres are there in 1 litre?
mcqs.why: The measuring jug shows that the 1000 ml mark is the same as 1 litre, so 1 litre = 1000 ml.

mcqs.q: A jug can hold 8 glasses of water. What is the capacity of the jug?
mcqs.why: Capacity is how much a container can hold. The jug holds 8 glasses of water, so its capacity is 8 glasses.

mcqs.q: A drink is filled to the 200 mark on the glass scale. How many millilitres is the drink?
mcqs.why: Read the scale at the top of the drink: it stops at 200, so the drink is 200 ml.

mcqs.q: How many millilitres are there in 2 litres?
mcqs.why: Each litre is 1000 ml: 2 × 1000 = 2000 ml.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used for the capacity of a fuel tank?
mcqs.why: A fuel tank holds a large amount of liquid, and large capacities are measured in litres.

mcqs.q: Which unit is used for a medicine dropper's amount?
mcqs.why: A dropper holds a very small amount of liquid, and small capacities are measured in millilitres.

mcqs.q: What is capacity?
options: The amount of liquid a container can hold
mcqs.why: Capacity tells us how much liquid a container can hold when it is full.

mcqs.q: A bottle holds 1000 tiny cups and each cup is 1 ml. What is the capacity of the bottle in millilitres?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 1000 cups × 1 ml = 1000 ml, which is the same as 1 litre.

mcqs.q: A measuring jug is filled to the 1000 ml mark. What is its capacity in litres?
mcqs.why: 1000 ml is exactly 1 litre, so the jug's capacity is 1 litre.

mcqs.q: A glass of soda holds 100 ml and a dropper holds 20 ml. Which holds more?
mcqs.why: Compare: 100 ml is more than 20 ml, so the glass of soda holds more.

lessons.title: Comparing Capacity and Capacity Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing capacities

Compare capacities in the same unit: a jug of 2 litres holds more than a juice packet of 1 litre; a fuel tank of 50 litres holds more than a tank of 20 litres; two containers of 500 litres each hold equal amounts.

Worked example

A juice manufacturer has 300 litres of apple juice and 50 litres of orange juice. How much juice is there in total?

Step 1: Join the two amounts: 300 + 50.

Answer: 350 litres

Worked example

A water tank can hold 500 litres of water. If 50 litres are poured out, how much water is left?

Step 1: Subtract: 500 − 50 = 450.

Answer: 450 litres

Key points

  • Add to join amounts; subtract when liquid is used or poured out.
  • A milk packet (250 ml) holds more than a juice packet (200 ml).
  • Tank A (60 L) holds less than tank B (65 L).

mcqs.q: A juice maker has 300 litres of apple juice and 50 litres of orange juice. How much juice is there in total?
mcqs.why: Join the apple juice and the orange juice: 300 + 50 = 350 litres.

mcqs.q: A pharmacist has 250 mL of medicine and adds 100 mL more. How much medicine is in the bottle now?
mcqs.why: More medicine is added to the bottle: 250 + 100 = 350 mL.

mcqs.q: A water tank holds 500 litres. If 50 litres are poured out, how much water is left?
mcqs.why: Water is poured out of the tank: 500 − 50 = 450 litres left.

mcqs.q: A juice packet has a capacity of 200 ml and another packet 100 ml. What is the total capacity of both packets?
mcqs.why: Join the capacities of both packets: 200 + 100 = 300 millilitres.

mcqs.q: A water tank has a capacity of 800 litres and a fuel tank 500 litres. What is the total capacity of both tanks?
mcqs.why: Join the capacities of both tanks: 800 + 500 = 1300 litres.

mcqs.q: A gas cylinder has a capacity of 45 litres. If 15 litres of gas are used, what capacity remains?
mcqs.why: Gas is used from the cylinder: 45 − 15 = 30 litres remain.

mcqs.q: A perfume bottle has a capacity of 100 ml. If 50 ml are used, how much perfume remains?
mcqs.why: Perfume is used from the bottle: 100 − 50 = 50 millilitres remain.

mcqs.q: A juice packet holds 200 ml and a milk packet holds 250 ml. Which has the greater capacity?
mcqs.why: Compare: 250 ml is more than 200 ml, so the milk packet has the greater capacity.

mcqs.q: Fuel tank A holds 60 litres and fuel tank B holds 65 litres. Which has the lesser capacity?
mcqs.why: Compare: 60 litres is less than 65 litres, so tank A has the lesser capacity.

mcqs.q: A water cooler holds 4 litres and a fuel gallon holds 4 litres. How do their capacities compare?
mcqs.why: Both hold 4 litres — the same amount — so their capacities are equal.

lessons.title: Temperature
lessons.notes_html:
Hot and cold

Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold something is. It is measured in degrees Centigrade (°C) with an instrument called a thermometer.

Reading a thermometer

Look at the mark where the red column stops — that mark is the temperature. On the temperature scale, the numbers grow as we move to the right, just like a number line: 0°C, 5°C, 10°C, 20°C and so on.

Worked example

The red column of a thermometer stops at the 25 mark. What is the temperature?

Step 1: Read the mark where the red column stops: 25.

Answer: 25°C

Key points

  • Unit of temperature: degree Centigrade (°C).
  • Instrument: thermometer.
  • Moving right on the scale means hotter; moving left means colder.

mcqs.q: In which unit is temperature measured?
mcqs.why: Temperature is measured in degrees Centigrade, written as °C.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is used to measure temperature?
mcqs.why: A thermometer is the instrument that measures how hot or cold something is.

mcqs.q: The red column of a thermometer stops at the 35 mark. What is the temperature in °C?
mcqs.why: Read the mark where the red column stops: 35, so the temperature is 35°C.

mcqs.q: The red column of a thermometer stops at the 45 mark. What is the temperature in °C?
mcqs.why: The column stops at the 45 mark, so the temperature is 45°C.

mcqs.q: The red column of a thermometer stops at the 60 mark. What is the temperature in °C?
mcqs.why: The column stops at the 60 mark, so the temperature is 60°C.

mcqs.q: The red column of a thermometer stops at the 80 mark. What is the temperature in °C?
mcqs.why: The column stops at the 80 mark, so the temperature is 80°C.

mcqs.q: The red column of a thermometer stops at the 95 mark. What is the temperature in °C?
mcqs.why: The column stops at the 95 mark, so the temperature is 95°C.

mcqs.q: On the temperature scale, what happens to the temperature as we move to the right?
mcqs.why: Like a number line, the numbers on the temperature scale get bigger to the right, so the temperature increases.

mcqs.q: Which temperature is hotter: 30°C or 45°C?
mcqs.why: 45 is greater than 30, so 45°C is the hotter temperature.

mcqs.q: Which temperature is colder: 15°C or 5°C?
mcqs.why: 5 is less than 15, so 5°C is the colder temperature.

lessons.title: Telling the Time on an Analog Clock
lessons.notes_html:
The two hands

An analog clock shows the time with hands on a face with numbers 1 to 12. The short hand points to the hour. The long hand points to the minutes.

Each number on the clock means 5 minutes for the long hand: multiply the number by 5 to get the minutes.

Worked example

The short hand is on 7 and the long hand is on 3. Tell the time.

Step 1: The short hand on 7 means the hour is 7.

Step 2: The long hand on 3 means 3 × 5 = 15 minutes.

Answer: 7:15 (7 hours and 15 minutes)

More examples

Short hand on 5, long hand on 8: 8 × 5 = 40 minutes, so the time is 5:40. Short hand just past 5, long hand on 9: 9 × 5 = 45, so the time is 5:45. When the long hand is on 12, it is an exact hour: short hand on 9 means 9:00.

Key points

  • Short hand = hours, long hand = minutes.
  • Minutes = clock number × 5.
  • Long hand on 12 means 0 minutes — an exact hour.

mcqs.q: The short hand is on 7 and the long hand is on 3. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 7 (short hand). The minutes are 3 × 5 = 15 (long hand on 3). So the time is 7:15.

mcqs.q: The short hand is on 5 and the long hand is on 8. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 5. The minutes are 8 × 5 = 40. So the time is 5:40.

mcqs.q: The short hand is on 6 and the long hand is on 7. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 6. The minutes are 7 × 5 = 35. So the time is 6:35.

mcqs.q: The short hand is on 12 and the long hand is on 2. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 12. The minutes are 2 × 5 = 10. So the time is 12:10.

mcqs.q: The short hand is just past 5 and the long hand is on 9. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 5 (the hand has just passed 5). The minutes are 9 × 5 = 45. So the time is 5:45.

mcqs.q: The short hand is between 10 and 11 and the long hand is on 6. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hour is 10 (the hand is between 10 and 11). The minutes are 6 × 5 = 30. So the time is 10:30.

mcqs.q: The short hand is on 9 and the long hand is on 12. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The long hand on 12 means 0 minutes — an exact hour. The short hand on 9 gives the time 9:00.

mcqs.q: The short hand is just before 7 and the long hand is on 10. What is the time?
mcqs.why: The hand just before 7 means the hour is still 6. The minutes are 10 × 5 = 50. So the time is 6:50.

mcqs.q: How many minutes does the number 4 on the clock show for the long hand?
mcqs.why: Each clock number means 5 minutes for the long hand: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes.

mcqs.q: Which hand of the clock shows the minutes?
mcqs.why: On an analog clock the long hand points to the minutes, and the short hand points to the hour.

lessons.title: Time Intervals
lessons.notes_html:
How long does it take?

A time interval (duration) is the time between a starting time and a finishing time. Count the minutes or hours from the start to the finish.

Worked example

A boy starts eating biryani at 2:00 pm and finishes at 2:15 pm. How long does he take?

Step 1: Both times are in the same hour, so count the minutes: from 2:00 to 2:15 is 15 minutes.

Answer: 15 minutes

Worked example

Boys start playing football at 5:00 pm and end the game at 7:00 pm. How long is the match?

Step 1: Count the hours: 5:00 → 6:00 → 7:00 is 2 hours.

Answer: 2 hours

Key points

  • Same hour: count minutes. Whole hours: count hours.
  • Ali's movie from 8:00 pm to 11:00 pm lasts 3 hours.
  • An artist drawing from 3:00 pm to 5:30 pm takes 2 hours and 30 minutes.

mcqs.q: A boy eats biryani from 2:00 pm to 2:15 pm. How many minutes does he take?
mcqs.why: Count the minutes from 2:00 to 2:15: 15 minutes.

mcqs.q: A football match starts at 5:00 pm and ends at 7:00 pm. How many hours does it last?
mcqs.why: Count the hours: 5:00 → 6:00 → 7:00. That is 2 hours.

mcqs.q: Ali watches a movie from 8:00 pm to 11:00 pm. How many hours does the movie last?
mcqs.why: Count the hours: 8:00 → 9:00 → 10:00 → 11:00. That is 3 hours.

mcqs.q: Khizar watches a cartoon from 6:00 pm to 6:30 pm. How many minutes does it last?
mcqs.why: Count the minutes from 6:00 to 6:30: 30 minutes.

mcqs.q: Asra goes on a trip from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm. How many hours is the trip?
mcqs.why: Count the hours: 10:00 → 11:00 → 12:00 → 1:00. That is 3 hours.

mcqs.q: An artist draws a picture from 3:00 pm to 5:30 pm. How long does he take?
mcqs.why: From 3:00 to 5:00 is 2 hours, and from 5:00 to 5:30 is 30 minutes more. Total: 2 hours and 30 minutes.

mcqs.q: Hina leaves Karachi at 9:00 am and arrives in Hyderabad at 11:00 pm. How many hours does she travel?
mcqs.why: Count the hours from 9:00 am: to 9:00 pm is 12 hours, then to 11:00 pm is 2 more hours. Total: 12 + 2 = 14 hours.

mcqs.q: A class starts at 9:00 am and ends at 9:45 am. How many minutes does it last?
mcqs.why: Count the minutes from 9:00 to 9:45: 45 minutes.

mcqs.q: A baby sleeps from 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm. How many hours does the baby sleep?
mcqs.why: Count the hours: 1:00 → 2:00 → 3:00 → 4:00. That is 3 hours.

mcqs.q: What is a time interval?
options: The time between a start time and a finish time
The time shown by the short hand
mcqs.why: A time interval (duration) tells how long something takes, counted from its starting time to its finishing time.

lessons.title: Days, Months and the Calendar
lessons.notes_html:
Days of the week

There are 7 days in a week: Monday (1st day), Tuesday (2nd), Wednesday (3rd), Thursday (4th), Friday (5th), Saturday (6th) and Sunday (7th). Tomorrow is the day after today; yesterday is the day before today.

Months of the year

There are 12 months in a year: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November and December.

Worked example

On the book's model calendar, Rida's birthday is on 13th October. Which day of the week will it be?

Step 1: Find October on the calendar and find the date 13.

Step 2: Read the day written above 13: it is in the Monday column.

Answer: Monday

Key points

  • To find a day, locate the date on the calendar and read the column heading.
  • The first Sunday of January on the model calendar is the 5th.
  • Independence Day (14th August) falls on Thursday on the model calendar.

mcqs.q: How many days are there in a week?
mcqs.why: The days of the week are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday — 7 days.

mcqs.q: How many months are there in a year?
mcqs.why: January to December are the months of the year. Count them: there are 12 months.

mcqs.q: Which day is the 5th day of the week?
mcqs.why: Count the days in order: Monday 1st, Tuesday 2nd, Wednesday 3rd, Thursday 4th, Friday 5th.

mcqs.q: If today is Friday, what day is tomorrow?
mcqs.why: Tomorrow is the day after today. The day after Friday is Saturday.

mcqs.q: If today is Friday, what day was yesterday?
mcqs.why: Yesterday is the day before today. The day before Friday is Thursday.

mcqs.q: Which month comes just after October?
mcqs.why: Read the months in order: ..., September, October, November, December. The month after October is November.

mcqs.q: On the model calendar, 13th October falls on which day?
mcqs.why: Find 13 in October on the book's model calendar: it is written in the Monday column.

mcqs.q: On the model calendar, the school's award ceremony on 2nd April falls on which day?
mcqs.why: Find 2 in April on the model calendar: it is in the Wednesday column.

mcqs.q: On the model calendar, the first Sunday of January is on which date?
mcqs.why: In January the Sundays are 5, 12, 19 and 26. The first Sunday is the 5th.

mcqs.q: On the model calendar, Independence Day (14th August) is celebrated on which day?
mcqs.why: Find 14 in August on the model calendar: August 1 is a Friday, and 14 falls in the Thursday column.

lessons.title: 2-D Shapes: Rectangle and Square
lessons.notes_html:
What is geometry?

Geometry is the branch of mathematics that deals with shapes, sizes and positions of objects. 2-D shapes are flat shapes that have only length and width.

The rectangle

A rectangle is a 2-D shape with four corners (vertices) and four sides (edges). All its sides are straight and the opposite sides are equal in length. The longer side is its length and the shorter side is its breadth (width). Example objects: a mobile, a door, a book.

The square

A square is a 2-D shape with four corners and four sides, but in a square all sides are equal. Example objects: a square clock face, an LCD, a Ludo board, a register.

Worked example

Draw a rectangle of length 10 cm and breadth 4 cm.

Step 1: Draw a straight top side of 10 cm.

Step 2: Draw 4 cm sides down from both corners.

Step 3: Join the bottom with another 10 cm side.

Answer: A rectangle with length 10 cm and breadth 4 cm

Key points

  • Rectangle: opposite sides equal. Square: all sides equal.
  • Both have 4 sides and 4 vertices.

mcqs.q: How many sides does a rectangle have?
mcqs.why: A rectangle is a four-sided shape: it has 4 sides (edges) and 4 corners.

mcqs.q: How many corners (vertices) does a square have?
mcqs.why: A square has four corners, called vertices — one at the end of each side.

mcqs.q: What is special about the sides of a square?
mcqs.why: In a square every side has the same length. This is what makes it different from a rectangle.

mcqs.q: What is special about the sides of a rectangle?
mcqs.why: In a rectangle the side facing another side has the same length: the two lengths are equal and the two breadths are equal.

mcqs.q: The longer side of a rectangle is called its ...?
mcqs.why: The longer side of a rectangle is its length, and the shorter side is its breadth or width.

mcqs.q: Which of these objects is square in shape?
mcqs.why: The book gives the Ludo board (and a square clock face, LCD and register) as square objects. A door, mobile and book are rectangles.

mcqs.q: Which of these objects is rectangular in shape?
mcqs.why: A door is longer than it is wide, with opposite sides equal — a rectangle. A ring and a pizza are circles.

mcqs.q: A square has each side 10 cm. How long is its third side?
mcqs.why: All sides of a square are equal, so if one side is 10 cm, every side — including the third — is 10 cm.

mcqs.q: What are 2-D shapes?
options: Shapes with length, width and height
Flat shapes with only length and width
Shapes with no sides at all
mcqs.why: 2-D (two-dimensional) shapes are flat: they have length and width only, like a circle or a square drawn on paper.

mcqs.q: What does geometry study?
options: Shapes, sizes and positions of objects
mcqs.why: Geometry is the branch of mathematics that deals with shapes, sizes and positions of objects.

lessons.title: Circle, Triangle, Semi-Circle and Quarter-Circle
lessons.notes_html:
The circle

A circle is a round-shaped figure with no corners and no edges. Example objects: a pizza, a clock, a ring. To draw one, make a dot and move the pencil round and round the dot.

The triangle

A triangle is a 2-D shape with three sides and three vertices. Example objects: an ice-cream cone, a triangular biscuit, a chocolate triangle.

Half and quarter circles

A semi-circle is half of a circle (1/2), made by cutting a circle into two halves: a speedometer, a protractor, a watermelon half-slice. A quarter-circle is one-fourth of a circle (1/4): a quarter slice of pizza.

Worked example

How many sides and vertices does a triangle have?

Step 1: Count the straight lines that make the shape: 3.

Step 2: Count the corners where the sides meet: 3.

Answer: 3 sides and 3 vertices

Key points

  • Circle: 0 corners, 0 edges.
  • Semi-circle = 1/2 of a circle; quarter-circle = 1/4 of a circle.

mcqs.q: How many corners does a circle have?
mcqs.why: A circle is a round curve with no corners and no edges at all.

mcqs.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
mcqs.why: A triangle is made of three straight sides joined at three corners.

mcqs.q: How many vertices does a triangle have?
mcqs.why: The sides of a triangle meet at three corners, so it has 3 vertices.

mcqs.q: A semi-circle is which part of a circle?
mcqs.why: Cutting a circle into two equal halves gives two semi-circles. Each one is half (1/2) of the circle.

mcqs.q: A quarter-circle is which part of a circle?
mcqs.why: Dividing a circle into four equal parts gives quarter-circles. Each one is one fourth (1/4) of the circle.

mcqs.q: Which object is an example of a circle?
mcqs.why: A ring is round with no corners — a circle. The book and Ludo board are rectangles/squares and the cone shape shown is a triangle.

mcqs.q: Which object is an example of a triangle?
mcqs.why: A triangular biscuit has 3 sides and 3 corners. The pizza and clock are circles, and the watermelon half-slice is a semi-circle.

mcqs.q: Which object is an example of a semi-circle?
mcqs.why: A protractor is shaped like half a circle — a semi-circle. A quarter slice of pizza is a quarter-circle.

mcqs.q: Which object is an example of a quarter-circle?
mcqs.why: A quarter slice is one of four equal parts of the pizza — a quarter-circle. A speedometer is a semi-circle.

mcqs.q: In the big picture of shapes, how many circles are there to colour red?
mcqs.why: Counting the circles in the book's big-circle picture: there are 4 circles (top, left, right and bottom), and all 4 are coloured red.

lessons.title: 3-D Shapes
lessons.notes_html:
Shapes with height too

A 3-D shape is an object that has length, width and height. We can see 3-D shapes from different angles. Some have flat surfaces, others are curved.

The five common 3-D shapes

Cube: six square faces of equal size — a dice, a Rubik's cube. Cuboid: six rectangular faces — a book, a brick, a match box, a milk carton.

Cone: a circular base and a curved surface that tapers to a point — an ice-cream cone, a party hat, a funnel. Cylinder: two circular bases joined by a curved surface — a water bottle, a gas cylinder, a tin of soft drink. Sphere: round and curved like a ball — a basketball, a globe, an orange.

Worked example

Which 3-D shape is a dice?

Step 1: A dice has six faces and every face is a square of equal size.

Answer: A cube

Key points

  • Cube: 6 equal square faces. Cuboid: 6 rectangular faces.
  • Cone: one point. Cylinder: two circular bases. Sphere: fully round.

mcqs.q: How many faces does a cube have?
mcqs.why: A cube has six faces, and every face is a square of equal size.

mcqs.q: Which 3-D shape is a dice?
mcqs.why: A dice has six equal square faces, so it is a cube.

mcqs.q: Which 3-D shape is a brick?
mcqs.why: A brick has six rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid — like a book or a match box.

mcqs.q: Which 3-D shape is an ice-cream cone?
mcqs.why: An ice-cream cone has a circular base and tapers to a point — that is a cone.

mcqs.q: Which 3-D shape is a tin of soft drink?
mcqs.why: A soft-drink tin has two circular bases joined by a curved surface — that is a cylinder.

mcqs.q: Which 3-D shape is a globe?
mcqs.why: A globe is round and curved on all sides like a ball — that is a sphere.

mcqs.q: What is special about a cone?
options: It has a circular base and tapers to a point
It is fully round like a ball
mcqs.why: A cone's curved surface narrows from its circular base up to one point, like a party hat.

mcqs.q: What is special about a cylinder?
options: It has two circular bases joined by a curved surface
It has no flat part at all
mcqs.why: A cylinder has a circle at the top and a circle at the bottom, joined by a curved surface — like a water bottle.

mcqs.q: Which object is a cuboid?
mcqs.why: A milk carton has six rectangular faces, so it is a cuboid. The basketball is a sphere, the party hat a cone and the gas cylinder a cylinder.

mcqs.q: How is a 3-D shape different from a 2-D shape?
options: It has height as well as length and width
mcqs.why: 3-D shapes have length, width and height, so we can hold them and see them from different angles. 2-D shapes are flat.

lessons.title: Position, Direction and Movement
lessons.notes_html:
Position words

Inside and outside: the book is inside the bag and the register is outside the bag. Above and below: the picture is above the sofa and below the clock. Over and under: a boy jumps over the hurdle and another crawls under it; a plane flies over the city. Far and near: the cow is near the house and the goat is far from the house.

Direction of turning

Clockwise means turning to the right, like a clock's hands moving from 12 to 3. Anti-clockwise means turning to the left, like the hands moving from 12 to 9. The Earth rotates around the Sun in the anti-clockwise direction.

Turns

Starting with an arrow pointing up: a quarter turn clockwise takes it to the right (3), a half turn takes it to the bottom (6), a three-quarter turn takes it to the left (9), and one whole turn brings it back to the top (12).

Key points

  • Clockwise = to the right; anti-clockwise = to the left.
  • Movement examples: the ball rolled around the corner; the bus went up the hill; the dog ran up the stairs.

mcqs.q: In the book's example, the book is inside the bag. Where is the register?
mcqs.why: The book's position example says: the book is inside the bag and the register is outside the bag.

mcqs.q: The picture hangs on the wall. The clock is at the top and the sofa is at the bottom. The picture is ...?
options: Above the clock and below the sofa
Above the sofa and below the clock
mcqs.why: The order on the wall is: clock at the top, then the picture, then the sofa. So the picture is below the clock and above the sofa.

mcqs.q: A plane is flying over the city. The word 'over' shows ...?
options: The plane is inside the city
The plane is under the city
The plane is far from the city
The plane is above the city, passing across it
mcqs.why: Over means above and across something, like the boy jumping over the hurdle.

mcqs.q: The cow is standing next to the house and the goat is a long way away. Which animal is near the house?
mcqs.why: Near means a short distance away. The cow is next to the house, so the cow is near; the goat is far.

mcqs.q: A clock's hands move from 12 to 3. In which direction are they turning?
mcqs.why: Moving from 12 to 3 is turning to the right, which is the clockwise direction — like a car wheel turning clockwise.

mcqs.q: A clock's hands move from 12 to 9. In which direction are they turning?
mcqs.why: Moving from 12 to 9 is turning to the left, which is the anti-clockwise direction.

mcqs.q: The Earth rotates around the Sun in which direction?
mcqs.why: The book gives the Earth's rotation around the Sun as the example of anti-clockwise movement.

mcqs.q: An arrow pointing up makes a quarter turn clockwise. Where does it point now?
mcqs.why: A quarter turn is one fourth of a full turn. Clockwise from the top, the arrow reaches the right side — the 3 position.

mcqs.q: An arrow pointing up makes a half turn clockwise. Where does it point now?
mcqs.why: A half turn is half of a full turn. From the top, the arrow reaches the opposite side — the bottom, the 6 position.

mcqs.q: An arrow makes one whole turn clockwise. Where does it end?
options: Back where it started, at the top
mcqs.why: One whole turn brings the arrow all the way around to its starting position — back at the top (12).

lessons.title: Pictographs
lessons.notes_html:
Pictures that show information

A pictograph is a special kind of graph that uses pictures to show information. To read it, count the pictures and multiply by the value of each picture.

Worked example

A pictograph shows favourite sports. Each student picture represents 1 student: Tennis has 1 picture, Football has 2 and Cricket has 3. How many students like each sport?

Step 1: Multiply the pictures by 1: Tennis 1 × 1 = 1, Football 2 × 1 = 2, Cricket 3 × 1 = 3.

Answer: Tennis 1, Football 2, Cricket 3 students

When each picture stands for more

If each picture represents 2 animals: Fish 2 pictures = 4, Cat 4 pictures = 8, Dog 5 pictures = 10. If each picture represents 4 vehicles: Bus 3 pictures = 12, Bicycle 4 pictures = 16, Car 6 pictures = 24.

Key points

  • Always check what one picture stands for.
  • Answer = number of pictures × value of one picture.

mcqs.q: In a pictograph each picture stands for 2 animals. Fish have 2 pictures. How many fish are there?
mcqs.why: Multiply the pictures by the value of one picture: 2 × 2 = 4 fish.

mcqs.q: In a pictograph each picture stands for 2 animals. Dogs have 5 pictures. How many dogs are there?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 5 pictures × 2 animals each = 10 dogs.

mcqs.q: In a pictograph each picture stands for 4 vehicles. Cars have 6 pictures. How many cars are there?
mcqs.why: Multiply the pictures by the value of each picture: 6 × 4 = 24 cars.

mcqs.q: In a pictograph each picture stands for 4 vehicles. Buses have 3 pictures. How many buses are there?
mcqs.why: Multiply the pictures by the value of each picture: 3 × 4 = 12 buses.

mcqs.q: In a traffic pictograph one picture stands for 2 vehicles. Cars have 5 pictures. How many cars passed?
mcqs.why: Multiply the pictures by the value of each picture: 5 × 2 = 10 cars.

mcqs.q: In a traffic pictograph one picture stands for 2 vehicles. Busses have 2 pictures. How many busses passed?
mcqs.why: Multiply the pictures by the value of each picture: 2 × 2 = 4 busses.

mcqs.q: In a traffic pictograph, vans are 8 and bicycles are 8. How many vans and bicycles passed altogether?
mcqs.why: Add the two amounts: 8 + 8 = 16 vehicles altogether.

mcqs.q: In a zoo pictograph each picture stands for 2 animals. Rabbits have 5 pictures. How many rabbits are there?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 5 × 2 = 10 rabbits — the most of any animal in the zoo pictograph.

mcqs.q: In the zoo pictograph there are 4 lions, 6 deer, 8 monkeys, 6 foxes, 10 rabbits and 2 elephants. How many animals are there altogether?
In the zoo pictograph there are 6 foxes and 2 elephants. How many more foxes are there than elephants?
mcqs.why: Subtract: 6 − 2 = 4 more foxes than elephants.

lessons.title: Block Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
Graphs made of blocks

A block graph uses blocks or bars to represent data. Each block represents a certain number of items, so count the blocks and multiply.

Worked example

A block graph shows Nasir's sleeping hours. Each block represents 1 hour: Sunday has 9 blocks, Monday has 7 blocks and Tuesday has 8 blocks. How many hours did Nasir sleep on each day?

Step 1: Multiply each day's blocks by 1: Sunday 9 × 1 = 9, Monday 7 × 1 = 7, Tuesday 8 × 1 = 8.

Answer: Sunday 9 hours, Monday 7 hours, Tuesday 8 hours

Blocks that stand for more

If each block represents 2 students: Red 5 blocks = 10 students, Blue 3 blocks = 6, Green 4 blocks = 8. If each block represents 3 students: Orange 8 blocks = 24, Apple 6 blocks = 18, Banana 4 blocks = 12.

Key points

  • Check the value of one block first.
  • Answer = number of blocks × value of one block.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 1 hour. Sunday has 9 blocks. How many hours is that?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 9 blocks × 1 hour each = 9 hours.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 2 students. Red has 5 blocks. How many students like red?
mcqs.why: Multiply the blocks by the value of each block: 5 × 2 = 10 students.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 2 students. Blue has 3 blocks. How many students like blue?
mcqs.why: Multiply the blocks by the value of each block: 3 × 2 = 6 students.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 3 students. Oranges have 8 blocks. How many students like oranges?
mcqs.why: Multiply the blocks by the value of each block: 8 × 3 = 24 students.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 3 students. Apples have 6 blocks. How many students like apples?
mcqs.why: Multiply the blocks by the value of each block: 6 × 3 = 18 students.

mcqs.q: In a block graph each block stands for 3 students. Bananas have 4 blocks. How many students like bananas?
mcqs.why: Multiply the blocks by the value of each block: 4 × 3 = 12 students.

mcqs.q: Nasir slept 9 hours on Sunday, 7 hours on Monday and 8 hours on Tuesday. On which day did he sleep the most?
mcqs.why: Compare the hours: 9 is more than 8 and 7. The greatest number is 9 hours (Sunday).

mcqs.q: In the colours graph, red has 10 students, blue has 6 and green has 8. How many students are there in all?
mcqs.why: Add the three colour groups together: 10 + 6 + 8 = 24 students.

mcqs.q: What is a block graph?
options: A graph made of pictures only
A graph that uses blocks or bars to represent data
mcqs.why: A block graph shows information with blocks or bars, where each block stands for a certain number of items.

mcqs.q: How do we find the value shown by a row of blocks?
options: Count the blocks and multiply by the value of one block
mcqs.why: Each block has a fixed value. The total is the number of blocks multiplied by the value of one block.

lessons.title: How Likely Is It?
lessons.notes_html:
Words for chances

We use special words to describe how likely something is to happen:

Impossible — it will never happen: a horse cannot fly; a cat cannot bark. Less likely — it is not very likely: a boy with a fracture in his foot is less likely to run. More likely — it has more chances to happen: a ball is more likely to bounce when dropped.

Unlikely — it has no chance to happen (as the book defines it): a car cannot fly. Certain — it will always happen: a ball will fall when dropped; night always comes after the day.

Worked example

What is the possibility of a dog meowing?

Step 1: Meowing is a cat's sound; a dog barks. A dog can never meow.

Answer: Impossible

Key points

  • Impossible = never. Certain = always.
  • A sunny day tomorrow is possible but not certain — it depends on the weather.
  • Getting one certain colour of candy from a mixed bag is less likely.

mcqs.q: What is the possibility of a cat barking?
mcqs.why: Barking is a dog's sound. A cat can never bark, so it is impossible.

mcqs.q: What is the possibility of a dog meowing?
mcqs.why: Meowing is a cat's sound and a dog barks. A dog can never meow, so it is impossible.

mcqs.q: What is the possibility of a ball bouncing when it is dropped?
mcqs.why: The book's example says a dropped ball has a strong chance to bounce, so it is more likely to bounce.

mcqs.q: What is the possibility of a ball falling when it is dropped?
mcqs.why: A dropped ball will always fall to the ground. Something that will always happen is certain.

mcqs.q: What is the possibility of getting a sunny day tomorrow?
mcqs.why: A sunny day can happen, but the weather can change, so it is possible yet not certain.

mcqs.q: A bag has candies of many colours. Getting one certain colour from the bag is ...?
mcqs.why: Because the bag holds many colours, the chance of picking one certain colour is small — it is less likely.

mcqs.q: A boy has a fracture in his foot. Running for him is ...?
mcqs.why: The book's example: a boy with a fracture in his foot is not very likely to run, so running is less likely for him.

mcqs.q: For a car to fly is ...?
options: Less likely to be seen daily
mcqs.why: As the book defines it, unlikely means having no chance to happen — a car cannot fly.

mcqs.q: Night coming after the day is ...?
mcqs.why: Night always comes after the day, without fail. Something that always happens is certain.

mcqs.q: What does 'impossible' mean?
mcqs.why: Impossible events have no chance at all: they will never happen, like a horse flying.

lessons.title: Workbook Addition Practice
lessons.notes_html:
What the workbook is for

The workbook gives short exercises to solve daily to make basic maths skills strong. It is a 15-minute activity during morning assembly time — one page per day — and after 4 days of exercises there is 1 assessment. Things to bring: pencil, eraser, colour pencils, textbook, notebook, slate and water bottle, all in the school bag.

Making a ten

To add numbers like 9 + 2, first make a ten: 9 needs 1 to make ten, so 9 + 2 = 9 + 1 + 1 = 11. In the same way 9 + 7 = 9 + 1 + 6 = 16.

Worked example

Add with carrying: 28 + 5.

Step 1: Ones: 8 + 5 = 13, write 3 and carry 1.

Step 2: Tens: 2 + 1 = 3.

Answer: 33

Key points

  • Make a ten first when adding to 9 or 8.
  • Add the ones first, then the tens.
  • All workbook answers match the book's answer key on page 208.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 2 + 4?
mcqs.why: Count all the dots in the workbook exercise together: 2 + 4 = 6.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 7 + 0?
mcqs.why: Adding zero keeps the number the same: 7 + 0 = 7.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (make a ten): What is 9 + 3?
mcqs.why: Make a ten first: 9 + 1 = 10, then add the remaining 2: 10 + 2 = 12. So 9 + 3 = 12.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (make a ten): What is 8 + 3?
mcqs.why: 8 needs 2 to make ten: 8 + 2 = 10, then add the remaining 1: 10 + 1 = 11. So 8 + 3 = 11.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (make a ten): What is 9 + 9?
mcqs.why: Make a ten: 9 + 1 = 10, then add the remaining 8: 10 + 8 = 18. So 9 + 9 = 18.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 45 + 24?
Workbook practice (with carrying): What is 48 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 1 = 5. So 48 + 9 = 57.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (with carrying): What is 39 + 26?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 6 = 15, write 5 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 39 + 26 = 65.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (with carrying): What is 69 + 21?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Tens: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. So 69 + 21 = 90.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (with carrying): What is 67 + 27?
mcqs.why: Ones: 7 + 7 = 14, write 4 and carry 1. Tens: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. So 67 + 27 = 94.

lessons.title: Workbook Subtraction Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Taking away in the workbook

The workbook practises subtraction step by step: first small numbers, then 2-digit numbers, then subtraction with borrowing.

Splitting to subtract

For 12 − 3, split 12 into 10 + 2 and take 3 from the 10 part: 12 − 3 = 9. For 15 − 8, count back or split: 15 − 5 = 10, then 10 − 3 = 7.

Worked example

Subtract with borrowing: 34 − 8.

Step 1: 8 cannot be taken from 4, so borrow 1 ten: 14 − 8 = 6.

Step 2: The tens become 2.

Answer: 26

Key points

  • Borrow 1 ten when the ones are too small.
  • After borrowing, the tens digit becomes one less.
  • 38 − 15 = 23: subtract ones (8 − 5 = 3), then tens (3 − 1 = 2).

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 8 − 3?
mcqs.why: Cross out 3 of the 8 stars: 5 are left. So 8 − 3 = 5.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 10 − 5?
mcqs.why: Take 5 away from 10 and count what is left over: 10 − 5 = 5.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (splitting): What is 12 − 3?
mcqs.why: Split 12 into 10 + 2 and take 3 from the ten: 10 − 3 = 7, then 7 + 2 = 9. So 12 − 3 = 9.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 15 − 8?
mcqs.why: Split 8 into 5 and 3: 15 − 5 = 10, then 10 − 3 = 7. So 15 − 8 = 7.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 19 − 6?
mcqs.why: Only the ones change: 9 − 6 = 3, and the ten stays. So 19 − 6 = 13.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 40 − 30?
mcqs.why: Subtract the tens: 4 tens − 3 tens = 1 ten = 10. So 40 − 30 = 10.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 38 − 15?
Workbook practice (with borrowing): What is 42 − 9?
mcqs.why: Borrow: 12 − 9 = 3, and the tens become 3. So 42 − 9 = 33.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (with borrowing): What is 54 − 17?
Workbook practice (with borrowing): What is 62 − 15?

lessons.title: Workbook Multiplication and Division Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Tables practice

The workbook practises the tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 in rows and in columns, and writes numbers as products in two ways: 15 = 3 × 5 = 5 × 3 and 12 = 3 × 4 = 4 × 3.

Sharing practice

Division is practised as equal sharing: 4 girls share 8 balls equally — 8 ÷ 4 = 2 balls for each girl. The reason comes from the tables: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 because 5 × 4 = 20.

Worked example

4 plates have 2 bananas on each plate. How many bananas are there in all?

Step 1: Add 2 four times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8, or multiply: 4 × 2 = 8.

Answer: 8 bananas

Key points

  • Multiplication and division are reverse of each other.
  • Level assessments mix all four operations: 6 × 3 = 18, 6 ÷ 3 = 2, 9 × 3 = 27, 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: 4 plates have 2 bananas each. How many bananas in all?
mcqs.why: Multiply: 4 × 2 = 8 bananas (2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8).

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 2 × 7?
Workbook practice: What is 5 × 9?
Workbook practice: What is 4 × 7?
Workbook practice: What is 10 × 9?
mcqs.why: Table of 10: write the number and add a zero: 10 × 9 = 90.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: 15 can be written as a product in two ways. Which pair is correct?
mcqs.why: Check: 3 × 5 = 15 and, changing the order, 5 × 3 = 15. Both products make 15.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: 4 girls share 8 balls equally. How many balls does each girl get?
mcqs.why: Share the balls equally among the 4 girls: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 balls each.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 20 ÷ 4?
mcqs.why: Use the table of 4 backwards: 4 × 5 = 20, so 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice: What is 16 ÷ 4?
mcqs.why: Use the table of 4 backwards: 4 × 4 = 16, so 16 ÷ 4 = 4.

mcqs.q: Workbook practice (level assessment): What is 63 ÷ 7?
mcqs.why: Think of the table: 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 ÷ 7 = 9.

lessons.title: Ordinal Numbers: Races and Traffic
lessons.notes_html:
Positions in the Urdu edition exercises

The Urdu edition of the book practises ordinal numbers with a frogs' row, an animal race and a line of traffic.

The animal race

The animals finish in this order: Horse 1st, Deer 2nd, Cheetah 3rd, Dog 4th, Lion 5th, Donkey 6th, Cat 7th, Camel 8th, Rabbit 9th, Zebra 10th, Elephant 11th and Cow 12th.

Worked example

Which position did the Cat get in the race?

Step 1: Count the animals in finishing order up to the Cat: Horse, Deer, Cheetah, Dog, Lion, Donkey, Cat — that is 7.

Answer: 7th

The traffic line

In the traffic picture, the yellow car is 1st, the red car is 2nd, the blue pickup is 3rd, the green van is 4th, the bus is 5th, the jeep is 6th and the bicycle is 18th.

Key points

  • Count positions from the front of the line or the finish of the race.
  • The Urdu edition also teaches number names up to 100.

mcqs.q: In the animal race, which position did the Cat get?
mcqs.why: Count the finishing order: Horse 1st, Deer 2nd, Cheetah 3rd, Dog 4th, Lion 5th, Donkey 6th, Cat 7th.

mcqs.q: In the animal race, which position did the Dog get?
mcqs.why: Count the finishing order: Horse 1st, Deer 2nd, Cheetah 3rd, Dog 4th.

mcqs.q: In the animal race, which position did the Lion get?
mcqs.why: Count the finishing order: after the Dog (4th) comes the Lion, so the Lion is 5th.

mcqs.q: In the animal race, which position did the Donkey get?
mcqs.why: Count the finishing order: the Donkey comes just after the Lion (5th), so the Donkey is 6th.

mcqs.q: In the frogs' row the positions shown are 1st, __, 3rd, __, __, 6th, __, 8th, __, 10th. Which ordinal number comes right after 3rd?
mcqs.why: Ordinal numbers come in order: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th. The number after 3rd is 4th.

mcqs.q: In the traffic line, which vehicle is 1st?
mcqs.why: Counting from the front of the traffic line, the first vehicle is the yellow car.

mcqs.q: In the traffic line, which vehicle is 5th?
mcqs.why: Count from the front: yellow car 1st, red car 2nd, blue pickup 3rd, green van 4th, bus 5th.

mcqs.q: In the traffic line, the bicycle is in which position?
mcqs.why: Counting all the vehicles in the picture, the bicycle is the 18th vehicle in the line.

mcqs.q: In the traffic line, the loader is the last vehicle. Which position is it?
mcqs.why: The traffic picture has 20 vehicles in all, and the loader is last, so it is in the 20th position.

mcqs.q: Which animal won the race (1st position)?
mcqs.why: The horse finished first in the animal race, so it is in the 1st position.

lessons.title: Place Value Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Ones, tens and hundreds practice

The Urdu edition practises place value with blocks and the abacus. A flat block is 100, a rod is 10 and a single block is 1.

Worked example

Write the number shown by 1 flat (100), 2 rods (tens) and 6 ones.

Step 1: Hundreds: 1 × 100 = 100.

Step 2: Tens: 2 × 10 = 20. Ones: 6.

Step 3: Add: 100 + 20 + 6 = 126.

Answer: 126

More practice

619 is made of 6 hundreds, 1 ten and 9 ones. In 54 there are 4 ones and 5 tens; in 96 there are 6 ones and 9 tens; 100 has 0 ones, 0 tens and 1 hundred. On the abacus, the beads give numbers like 252, 404, 365 and 128.

Key points

  • Read the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.
  • The middle digit of 946 is 4, and its place value is 40.

mcqs.q: What number is made by 1 hundred, 2 tens and 6 ones?
mcqs.why: Add the hundreds, tens and ones together: 100 + 20 + 6 = 126.

mcqs.q: What number is made by 6 hundreds, 1 ten and 9 ones?
mcqs.why: Add the hundreds, tens and ones together: 600 + 10 + 9 = 619.

mcqs.q: How many ones are there in the number 54?
mcqs.why: 54 = 5 tens + 4 ones. The ones digit is 4, so there are 4 ones.

mcqs.q: How many tens are there in the number 96?
mcqs.why: 96 = 9 tens + 6 ones. The tens digit is 9, so there are 9 tens.

mcqs.q: What number do blocks for 237 show in hundreds, tens and ones? (hundreds digit)
mcqs.why: 237 has 2 hundreds, 3 tens and 7 ones, so the hundreds digit is 2.

mcqs.q: On the abacus, the beads show 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 4 ones. What is the number?
mcqs.why: Add the hundreds, tens and ones together: 400 + 0 + 4 = 404.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the middle (tens) digit in 946?
mcqs.why: The middle digit of 946 is 4. It is in the tens place, so its place value is 4 × 10 = 40.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the middle (tens) digit in 698?
mcqs.why: The middle digit of 698 is 9. It is in the tens place, so its place value is 9 × 10 = 90.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of the middle (tens) digit in 501?
mcqs.why: The middle digit of 501 is 0. Zero tens have a place value of 0.

mcqs.q: What number is shown by blocks: 6 hundreds flats and 5 tens rods only?
mcqs.why: 6 hundreds = 600 and 5 tens = 50, with no ones: 600 + 50 + 0 = 650.

lessons.title: Comparing and Ordering Practice
lessons.notes_html:
More comparing practice

The Urdu edition practises finding the smaller and bigger number in pairs: compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.

Worked example

Which is smaller: 149 or 184?

Step 1: Both have 1 hundred. Compare the tens: 4 tens against 8 tens.

Step 2: 4 tens is less than 8 tens.

Answer: 149 is smaller

Ordering practice

Ascending rows like 7, 19, 41, 50 go up; descending rows like 94, 72, 61, 50 go down. Counting in tens: 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 300. Counting in hundreds: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500.

Key points

  • Among 112, 132, 141, 162, 150, 126: the smallest is 112 and the biggest is 162.
  • Count back 10 numbers from 90: 90, 89, ..., 81.

mcqs.q: Which is the smaller number: 149 or 184?
mcqs.why: Both have 1 hundred. Tens: 4 tens is less than 8 tens, so 149 is smaller.

mcqs.q: Which is the bigger number: 165 or 169?
mcqs.why: Both start with 16. Ones: 9 is greater than 5, so 169 is bigger.

mcqs.q: Which is the smaller number: 21 or 61?
mcqs.why: Compare the tens: 2 tens is less than 6 tens, so 21 is smaller.

mcqs.q: Which is the bigger number: 910 or 210?
mcqs.why: Compare the hundreds: 9 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds, so 910 is bigger.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest number in the group 112, 132, 141, 162, 150, 126?
mcqs.why: Compare the tens digits: 112 has the smallest tens digit (1) among the numbers starting with 1, so 112 is the smallest.

mcqs.q: What is the biggest number in the group 112, 132, 141, 162, 150, 126?
mcqs.why: Compare the tens digits: 162 has the biggest tens digit (6), so 162 is the biggest.

mcqs.q: Which row is in ascending (increasing) order?
mcqs.why: In 7, 19, 41, 50 every number is bigger than the one before it, so the row is in ascending order.

mcqs.q: Which row is in descending (decreasing) order?
mcqs.why: In 94, 72, 61, 50 every number is smaller than the one before it, so the row is in descending order.

mcqs.q: Count in tens: 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, __. What number comes next?
mcqs.why: Each step adds one ten: after 290 comes 300.

mcqs.q: Count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300, 400, __. What number comes next?
mcqs.why: Each step adds one hundred: after 400 comes 500.

lessons.title: Half, One-Third and One-Quarter
lessons.notes_html:
Equal parts of a whole

The Urdu edition practises fractions with equal parts. A shape has equal parts only when all its parts are the same size. A bead string with parts of 3, 4 and 3 beads does NOT have equal parts, because 4 is not equal to 3.

Names of the parts

One of 2 equal parts is a half (1/2). One of 3 equal parts is one-third (1/3). One of 4 equal parts is one-quarter (1/4). The Urdu edition's table of unit fractions goes from 1/2 up to 1/12.

Worked example

A circle is divided into 8 equal parts and 1 part is coloured. What fraction is coloured?

Step 1: Coloured parts = 1. Total equal parts = 8.

Answer: 1/8

Key points

  • A bar in 3 parts with 2 green parts shows 2/3.
  • A grid in 4 parts with 3 yellow parts shows 3/4.
  • An orange circle cut into 2 UNEQUAL parts has 0 equal parts.

mcqs.q: A shape is divided into 2 equal parts. One part is called ...?
mcqs.why: When a whole is divided into 2 equal parts, each part is one half, written 1/2.

mcqs.q: A shape is divided into 3 equal parts. One part is called ...?
mcqs.why: When a whole is divided into 3 equal parts, each part is one-third, written 1/3.

mcqs.q: A shape is divided into 4 equal parts. One part is called ...?
mcqs.why: When a whole is divided into 4 equal parts, each part is one-quarter, written 1/4.

mcqs.q: A circle is divided into 8 equal parts and 1 part is coloured. What fraction is coloured?
mcqs.why: Coloured parts = 1 and total equal parts = 8, so the coloured fraction is 1/8 — a unit fraction.

mcqs.q: A grid is divided into 9 equal parts and 1 part is coloured. What fraction is coloured?
mcqs.why: Coloured parts = 1 and total equal parts = 9, so the fraction is 1/9.

mcqs.q: A bar is divided into 3 equal parts and 2 parts are green. What fraction is green?
mcqs.why: Green parts = 2 and total parts = 3, so the green fraction is 2/3 — a non-unit fraction.

mcqs.q: A grid is divided into 4 equal parts and 3 parts are yellow. What fraction is yellow?
mcqs.why: Yellow parts = 3 and total parts = 4, so the yellow fraction is 3/4.

mcqs.q: A circle is divided into 5 equal parts and 4 parts are green. What fraction is green?
mcqs.why: Green parts = 4 and total parts = 5, so the green fraction is 4/5.

mcqs.q: A bead string has parts of 3, 4 and 3 beads. Are its parts equal?
mcqs.why: Equal parts must all be the same size. The parts are 3, 4 and 3, and 4 is not equal to 3, so the parts are not equal.

mcqs.q: An orange circle is cut into 2 unequal parts. How many equal parts does it have?
mcqs.why: The two parts are not the same size, so the circle has no equal parts at all: 0 equal parts.

lessons.title: Adding Two-Digit Numbers with Carrying
lessons.notes_html:
Carrying in the Urdu edition

The Urdu edition practises adding when the ones make more than 9: write the ones digit and carry the ten.

Worked example

Add 28 + 9.

Step 1: Ones: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7 and carry 1.

Step 2: Tens: 2 + 1 (carried) = 3.

Answer: 37

More practice

Two-digit plus two-digit: 35 + 46 — ones: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1, carry 1; tens: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8, so the answer is 81.

Key points

  • Always add the ones first.
  • The colour-by-sum flower checks sums from 10 (brown) to 17 (sky blue).

mcqs.q: What is 28 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7 and carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 = 3. So 28 + 9 = 37.

mcqs.q: What is 34 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 4 + 9 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 1 = 4. So 34 + 9 = 43.

mcqs.q: What is 36 + 5?
mcqs.why: Ones: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 1 = 4. So 36 + 5 = 41.

mcqs.q: What is 47 + 7?
mcqs.why: Ones: 7 + 7 = 14, write 4 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 1 = 5. So 47 + 7 = 54.

mcqs.q: What is 88 + 8?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 + 8 = 16, write 6 and carry 1. Tens: 8 + 1 = 9. So 88 + 8 = 96.

mcqs.q: What is 83 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 3 + 9 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Tens: 8 + 1 = 9. So 83 + 9 = 92.

mcqs.q: What is 18 + 12?
mcqs.why: Ones: 8 + 2 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Tens: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. So 18 + 12 = 30.

mcqs.q: What is 25 + 19?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 9 = 14, write 4 and carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. So 25 + 19 = 44.

mcqs.q: What is 35 + 46?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. So 35 + 46 = 81.

mcqs.q: What is 39 + 58?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and carry 1. Tens: 3 + 5 + 1 = 9. So 39 + 58 = 97.

lessons.title: Adding Three-Digit Numbers without Carrying
lessons.notes_html:
No carrying needed

When every column adds to 9 or less, just add the columns one by one: ones, tens, hundreds.

Worked example

Add 195 + 3.

Step 1: Ones: 5 + 3 = 8. Tens: 9 + 0 = 9. Hundreds: 1.

Answer: 198

Checking statements

Some given answers must be checked: 703 + 20 = 723 is correct, and 463 + 12 = 475 is correct, but 119 + 50 = 159 is WRONG — the correct sum is 169.

Key points

  • Add column by column from the ones.
  • Always check a given answer before ticking it.

mcqs.q: What is 195 + 3?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 3 = 8. Tens and hundreds stay: 195 + 3 = 198.

mcqs.q: What is 174 + 4?
mcqs.why: Ones: 4 + 4 = 8. The rest stays: 174 + 4 = 178.

mcqs.q: What is 363 + 6?
mcqs.why: Ones: 3 + 6 = 9. The rest stays: 363 + 6 = 369.

mcqs.q: What is 437 + 2?
mcqs.why: Ones: 7 + 2 = 9. The rest stays: 437 + 2 = 439.

mcqs.q: What is 531 + 7?
mcqs.why: Ones: 1 + 7 = 8. The rest stays: 531 + 7 = 538.

mcqs.q: What is 710 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 0 + 9 = 9. The rest stays: 710 + 9 = 719.

mcqs.q: What is 812 + 6?
mcqs.why: Ones: 2 + 6 = 8. The rest stays: 812 + 6 = 818.

mcqs.q: What is 900 + 7?
mcqs.why: Ones: 0 + 7 = 7. The rest stays: 900 + 7 = 907.

mcqs.q: Is this statement correct? 703 + 20 = 723
mcqs.why: Check: ones 3 + 0 = 3, tens 0 + 2 = 2, hundreds 7. So 703 + 20 = 723. The statement is correct.

mcqs.q: Is this statement correct? 119 + 50 = 159
mcqs.why: Check: ones 9 + 0 = 9, tens 1 + 5 = 6, hundreds 1. So 119 + 50 = 169, not 159. The statement is wrong.

lessons.title: Adding Three-Digit Numbers with Carrying
lessons.notes_html:
Carrying with bigger numbers

With three-digit numbers, a column can carry into the tens or into the hundreds. Sometimes the sum goes past 999 and becomes a four-digit number.

Worked example

Add 397 + 8.

Step 1: Ones: 7 + 8 = 15, write 5 and carry 1.

Step 2: Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1.

Step 3: Hundreds: 3 + 1 = 4.

Answer: 405

Worked example

Add 999 + 41.

Step 1: Ones: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1.

Step 2: Tens: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4 and carry 1.

Step 3: Hundreds: 9 + 1 = 10.

Answer: 1040

Key points

  • Carry step by step, column by column.
  • 999 + 9 = 1008 — the answer can have four digits.

mcqs.q: What is 397 + 8?
mcqs.why: Ones: 7 + 8 = 15, write 5, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Hundreds: 3 + 1 = 4. So 397 + 8 = 405.

mcqs.q: What is 299 + 7?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. So 299 + 7 = 306.

mcqs.q: What is 999 + 9?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 9 = 18, write 8, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Hundreds: 9 + 1 = 10. So 999 + 9 = 1008.

mcqs.q: What is 593 + 7?
mcqs.why: Ones: 3 + 7 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Hundreds: 5 + 1 = 6. So 593 + 7 = 600.

mcqs.q: What is 196 + 45?
mcqs.why: Ones: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4, carry 1. Hundreds: 1 + 1 = 2. So 196 + 45 = 241.

mcqs.q: What is 287 + 37?
mcqs.why: Ones: 7 + 7 = 14, write 4, carry 1. Tens: 8 + 3 + 1 = 12, write 2, carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3. So 287 + 37 = 324.

mcqs.q: What is 654 + 68?
mcqs.why: Ones: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2, carry 1. Tens: 5 + 6 + 1 = 12, write 2, carry 1. Hundreds: 6 + 1 = 7. So 654 + 68 = 722.

mcqs.q: What is 999 + 41?
mcqs.why: Ones: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14, write 4, carry 1. Hundreds: 9 + 1 = 10. So 999 + 41 = 1040.

mcqs.q: What is 495 + 15?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0, carry 1. Tens: 9 + 1 + 1 = 11, write 1, carry 1. Hundreds: 4 + 1 = 5. So 495 + 15 = 510.

mcqs.q: What is 234 + 679?
mcqs.why: Ones: 4 + 9 = 13, write 3, carry 1. Tens: 3 + 7 + 1 = 11, write 1, carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 6 + 1 = 9. So 234 + 679 = 913.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems and the Order of Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Joining amounts in stories

Word problems about two amounts together are solved by adding. Read the story, pick the two numbers and add them in columns.

The order of addition

Changing the order of the numbers does not change the sum: 4 mangoes + 5 mangoes = 5 mangoes + 4 mangoes = 9 mangoes. In numbers: 27 + 12 = 12 + 27 = 39 and 28 + 22 = 22 + 28 = 50. This is called the commutative property of addition.

Worked example

Adil has 242 balloons. His friend has 123 balloons. How many balloons do they have in all?

Step 1: Ones: 2 + 3 = 5. Tens: 4 + 2 = 6. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3.

Answer: 365 balloons

Key points

  • "In all", "altogether" and "total" mean add.
  • Order never changes an addition answer.

mcqs.q: Zainab scored 28 marks in English and 18 marks in Mathematics. How many marks did she score in all?
mcqs.why: Add the two scores: ones 8 + 8 = 16, write 6, carry 1; tens 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. So 28 + 18 = 46 marks.

mcqs.q: A plant had 49 buds. Then 37 more buds grew. How many buds are there in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 9 + 7 = 16, write 6, carry 1; tens 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. So 49 + 37 = 86 buds.

mcqs.q: Ali scored 64 runs in the first match and 27 runs in the second match. How many runs did he score in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 4 + 7 = 11, write 1, carry 1; tens 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. So 64 + 27 = 91 runs.

mcqs.q: A library has 215 books on one shelf and 271 books on another shelf. How many books are there in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 5 + 1 = 6; tens 1 + 7 = 8; hundreds 2 + 2 = 4. So 215 + 271 = 486 books.

mcqs.q: Aryan has 331 cards and his sister has 625 cards. How many cards do they have in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 1 + 5 = 6; tens 3 + 2 = 5; hundreds 3 + 6 = 9. So 331 + 625 = 956 cards.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sold 159 buttons in the morning and 244 buttons in the evening. How many buttons did he sell in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 9 + 4 = 13, write 3, carry 1; tens 5 + 4 + 1 = 10, write 0, carry 1; hundreds 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. So 159 + 244 = 403 buttons.

mcqs.q: A factory filled 376 litres of water in the morning and 465 litres in the evening. How many litres were filled in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 6 + 5 = 11, write 1, carry 1; tens 7 + 6 + 1 = 14, write 4, carry 1; hundreds 3 + 4 + 1 = 8. So 376 + 465 = 841 litres.

mcqs.q: Two friends collected 586 rupees and 579 rupees for a fair. How much money did they collect in all?
mcqs.why: Add: ones 6 + 9 = 15, write 5, carry 1; tens 8 + 7 + 1 = 16, write 6, carry 1; hundreds 5 + 5 + 1 = 11. So 586 + 579 = 1165 rupees.

mcqs.q: What is 27 + 12? (Use the order rule to check with 12 + 27.)
mcqs.why: 27 + 12 = 39. Changing the order gives 12 + 27 = 39 — the same sum, by the commutative property of addition.

mcqs.q: What is 45 + 35?
mcqs.why: Ones: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. So 45 + 35 = 80 (and 35 + 45 is also 80).

lessons.title: Subtraction with Borrowing (Two-Digit Numbers)
lessons.notes_html:
Borrowing a ten

When the ones digit on top is smaller than the ones digit below, borrow 1 ten from the tens: the number 23 becomes 1 ten and 13 ones, so 23 − 7 can be done as 13 − 7 = 6 ones and 1 ten left — the answer is 16.

Worked example

Subtract 37 − 9.

Step 1: 9 cannot be taken from 7, so borrow 1 ten: 17 − 9 = 8.

Step 2: The tens become 3 − 1 = 2.

Answer: 28

Worked example

Subtract 76 − 47.

Step 1: Ones: borrow, 16 − 7 = 9.

Step 2: Tens: 6 − 4 = 2.

Answer: 29

Key points

  • After borrowing, the tens digit becomes one less.
  • On the abacus: 35 − 8 = 27 and 40 − 6 = 34.

mcqs.q: What is 23 − 7?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 ten: 23 = 1 ten + 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 1. So 23 − 7 = 16.

mcqs.q: What is 37 − 9?
mcqs.why: Borrow: 17 − 9 = 8, and the tens become 2. So 37 − 9 = 28.

mcqs.q: What is 43 − 5?
mcqs.why: Borrow: 13 − 5 = 8, and the tens become 3. So 43 − 5 = 38.

mcqs.q: What is 85 − 7?
mcqs.why: Borrow: 15 − 7 = 8, and the tens become 7. So 85 − 7 = 78.

mcqs.q: What is 35 − 8?
mcqs.why: Borrow: 15 − 8 = 7, and the tens become 2. So 35 − 8 = 27 (the abacus activity answer).

mcqs.q: What is 32 − 15?
What is 70 − 25?
What is 76 − 47?
What is 42 − 24?
What is 90 − 82?
mcqs.why: Ones: 0 − 2 cannot be done, borrow: 10 − 2 = 8. Tens: 8 − 8 = 0. So 90 − 82 = 8.

lessons.title: Subtracting Three-Digit Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Bigger subtractions

Three-digit subtraction works column by column. Borrowing can be needed in the ones, in the tens, or across a zero.

Worked example

Subtract 705 − 8 (borrowing across zero).

Step 1: The tens are 0, so borrow from the hundreds: the 7 hundreds become 6, the tens become 10, then lend one ten to the ones: ones become 15.

Step 2: Ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 9 − 0 = 9. Hundreds: 6.

Answer: 697

Worked example

Subtract 582 − 294.
